worked_solution:
Solving $x-3z=0$ for $x,$ we get $x=3z.$ Solving $y+w=0$ for $w,$ we get $w=-y.$  Therefore, any vector from $\text{Ker}(T)$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}3z \\ y \\ z \\ -y\end{aligned}]=z{{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{1}}+y{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{v}_{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $\text{Ker}(T)=\text{Span}{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}.$ Therefore, $\text{nullity}(T)=2.$ 

Finally, according the rank-nullity theorem, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{rank}(T) & =4-\text{nullity}(T) \\  & =4-2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
